q: The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position (or) equilibrium line are called wave crest and wave trough respectively.
e: True. The highest and the lowest points which show the maximum displacement of vibrating particle from its rest position (or) equilibrium line are called wave crest and wave trough respectively. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The highest point is called wave trough and the lowest point is called wave crest.
e: False. The highest point is the crest and the lowest is the trough. Those names are not swapped.

q: Wavelength ($\lambda$): The distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) two consecutive wave troughs is called wavelength.
e: True. Wavelength ($\lambda$): The distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) two consecutive wave troughs is called wavelength. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: The unit of wavelength in SI unit is centimetre (cm).
e: False. The unit of wavelength in SI unit is metre (m). This claim used centimetre (cm) in place of metre (m).

q: The unit of wavelength in SI unit is metre (m).
e: True. The unit of wavelength in SI unit is metre (m). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: Generally the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of same phase.
e: True. Generally the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of same phase. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.

q: Frequency ($f$): The number of complete waves passing a point per second of a vibrating source in one second is also called frequency.
e: True. Frequency ($f$): The number of complete waves passing a point per second of a vibrating source in one second is also called frequency. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The SI unit of frequency is hertz (Hz).
e: True. The SI unit of frequency is hertz (Hz). SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per minute.
e: False. One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second. This claim used minute in place of second.

q: One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second.
e: True. One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second. Every quantity named in that sentence is being used in its physics sense.

q: Period ($T$): The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) the time required for one complete vibration is called period of a wave.
e: True. Period ($T$): The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests (or) the time required for one complete vibration is called period of a wave. Period is the time for one complete vibration.

q: The unit of period is the minute (min).
e: False. The unit of period is the second (s). This claim used minute (min) in place of second (s).

q: The unit of period is the second (s).
e: True. The unit of period is the second (s). The unit of period is the second is the time for one complete vibration.

q: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency.
e: True. The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The relationship between period and frequency is $T = f$.
e: False. The relationship between period and frequency is $T = \frac{1}{f}$. This claim used f$ in place of \frac{1}{f}$.

q: The relationship between period and frequency is $T = \frac{1}{f}$.
e: True. The relationship between period and frequency is $T = \frac{1}{f}$. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: Amplitude: The amplitude of a wave is the maximum value of displacement of vibrating particle.
e: True. Amplitude: The amplitude of a wave is the maximum value of displacement of vibrating particle. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: Velocity of Wave ($v$): Velocity of wave is the speed with which a wave crest travels.
e: True. Velocity of Wave ($v$): Velocity of wave is the speed with which a wave crest travels. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The unit of wave velocity is metre per second ($\text{ms}^{-1}$).
e: True. The unit of wave velocity is metre per second ($\text{ms}^{-1}$). Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine (or) cosine graphs.
